questions.question: If a + (1)/(a) = 3, then find the value of a⁶ + (1)/(a⁶)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: a + 1/a = 3

Shortcut: Use the identity: a⁶ + 1/a⁶ = (a² + 1/a²)³ − 3(a² + 1/a²).

First, a² + 1/a² = (a + 1/a)² − 2 = 3² − 2 = 7.

Now, a⁶ + 1/a⁶ = 7³ − 3(7) = 343 − 21 = 322.

**∴ Answer = 322**

questions.question:
Consider the following statements.

1. Before the Prime Minister enters upon his office, the President administers to him the oaths of office and secrecy.

2. The President can dismiss the Prime Minister at any time in an arbitrary way.

3. If the Prime Minister loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha, he must resign or the President can dismiss him.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 3 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Before the **Prime Minister** enters upon his office, the **President** administers to him the **oaths of office and secrecy**. In his oath of office, the **Prime Minister** swears to bear true faith and allegiance to the **Constitution of India**, to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, and to faithfully discharge the duties of his office. In his oath of secrecy, he swears that he will not directly or indirectly communicate or reveal any matter that is brought under his consideration. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **President** can dismiss the **Prime Minister** at any time in an arbitrary way. This is a misunderstanding of the constitutional provision. Although **Article 75** states that the **Prime Minister** shall hold office during the **pleasure of the President**, this pleasure is not arbitrary. So long as the **Prime Minister** enjoys the **majority support** in the **Lok Sabha** (the **Lower House** of **Parliament**), the **President** cannot dismiss him. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• If the **Prime Minister** loses the confidence of the **Lok Sabha**, he must resign or the **President** can dismiss him. This is based on the principle of **Collective Responsibility** mentioned in **Article 75** of the **Constitution of India**. If a **No-Confidence Motion** is passed against the government in the **Lok Sabha**, the entire **Council of Ministers**, including the **Prime Minister**, must resign. If they fail to do so, the **President** has the constitutional power to dismiss the government. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the real executive authority (**de facto executive**) while the **President** is the nominal executive authority (**de jure executive**). The **Prime Minister** acts as the head of the **Union Council of Ministers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• **Article 74:** There shall be a **Council of Ministers** with the **Prime Minister** at the head to aid and advise the **President** who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice.
 
• **Article 75:** The **Prime Minister** shall be appointed by the **President** and the other **Ministers** shall be appointed by the **President** on the advice of the **Prime Minister**.
 
• **Article 78:** It defines the duties of the **Prime Minister** in respect of the furnishing of information to the **President**, including communicating all decisions of the **Council of Ministers** relating to the administration of the affairs of the **Union**.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility and Appointment:**
 
 
• To become the **Prime Minister** of India, a person must be a citizen of India and a member of either the **Lok Sabha** or the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• If the person is a member of the **Lok Sabha**, the minimum **age** should be **25 years**, and if he/she is a member of the **Rajya Sabha**, the **age** should be **30 years**.
 
• A person who is not a member of either House of **Parliament** can also be appointed as **Prime Minister** for **6 months**, within which he/she must get elected to either House.
 
 
 
• **Powers and Functions:**
 
 
• The **Prime Minister** allocates and reshuffles various portfolios among the **Ministers**.
 
• He presides over the meeting of the **Council of Ministers** and influences its decisions.
 
• He is the principal channel of communication between the **President** and the **Council of Ministers**.
 
• He advises the **President** with regard to the appointment of important officials like the **Attorney General of India**, **Comptroller and Auditor General of India** (**CAG**), and Chairmen of the **UPSC**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Term of Office:** The term of the **Prime Minister** is not fixed by the **Constitution**. He holds office as long as he enjoys the support of the **majority** in the **Lok Sabha**. Generally, this coincides with the life of the **Lok Sabha**, which is **5 years**.
 
• **Ex-officio Positions:** The **Prime Minister** is the **Chairman** of the **NITI Aayog** (which replaced the **Planning Commission** on **January 1, 2015**), the **National Development Council**, the **National Integration Council**, the **Inter-State Council**, and the **National Water Resources Council**.
 
• **Historical Context:** **Jawaharlal Nehru** was the first **Prime Minister** of India, serving from **1947** to **1964**. **Gulzarilal Nanda** was the first **Acting Prime Minister**. **Indira Gandhi** was the first woman **Prime Minister**.
 
• **Salary and Allowances:** The salary and allowances of the **Prime Minister** are determined by the **Parliament** from time to time. He receives the same salary and allowances as are payable to a **Member of Parliament**, plus a sumptuary allowance and other perks.

questions.question: Find the value of y, satisfying 22 × 3 × 816 ÷ √ 2601 = y + 794
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ √2601 = 51

⇒ 816 ÷ 51 = 16

⇒ 22 × 3 × 16 = 22 × 48 = 1056

⇒ y = 1056 − 794 = 262

**∴ Answer = 262**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

22 × 3 × 816 ÷ √2601 = y + 794

**Concept Used:**

BODMAS rule

**Calculation:**

⇒ 22 × 3 × 816 ÷ 51 = y + 794

⇒ 22 × 3 × 16 = y + 794

⇒ 22 × 48 = y + 794

⇒ 1056 = y + 794

⇒ y = 1056 − 794

⇒ y = 262

**∴ The correct answer is 262.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Perfect Square:** √2601 = 51, useful for fast simplification.

**BODMAS Rule:** Follow correct order: division and multiplication before addition.

**Cancellation:** 816 ÷ 51 simplifies early to reduce calculation load.

**Linear Equation:** Solve y + constant = value by shifting constant to RHS.

questions.question: 100 men have provisions for 27 days. If 50 men have left, for how many days the same provisions would last for the remaining men?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Total food = 100 × 27 = 2700 man-days

⇒ Remaining men = 50

⇒ Days = 2700 ÷ 50 = 54

**∴ Answer = 54 days**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

100 men → 27 days

50 men → ? days

**Concept Used:**

Men × Days = Constant (Total work/food)

**Calculation:**

⇒ 100 × 27 = 50 × x

⇒ 2700 = 50x

⇒ x = 2700 ÷ 50

⇒ x = 54

**∴ The correct answer is 54 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Man-Days Concept:** Total work = Men × Days remains constant.

**Inverse Proportion:** More men → fewer days, fewer men → more days.

**LCM Method:** Assume total work as LCM for faster calculation in exams.

**Shortcut Tip:** Directly divide total man-days by remaining men.

questions.question: A shopkeeper professes to sell his goods at a 45% loss but uses a false balance and gains 50%. The actual weight (rounded off to one decimal place) that he uses instead of 1 kg is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Assume CP of 1 kg = 100

⇒ 45% loss ⇒ SP = 55

⇒ Overall gain = 50% ⇒ Effective SP = 150

⇒ So, 55 price is actually for weight = 55/150 kg

⇒ = 0.3667 kg = 366.7 gm

**∴ Answer = 366.7 gm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss = 45%

Gain due to false weight = 50%

**Concept Used:**

Net gain when false weight is used

**Calculation:**

⇒ Assume CP of 1 kg = 100

⇒ Due to 45% loss, SP of 1 kg = 55

⇒ Let actual weight given = x kg

⇒ CP of x kg = 100x

⇒ Profit % = 50%

⇒ SP = 1.5 × CP = 1.5 × 100x = 150x

⇒ But SP = 55

⇒ 150x = 55

⇒ x = 55 ÷ 150

⇒ = 0.3667 kg = 366.7 gm

**∴ The correct answer is **366.7 gm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**False Weight Trick:** Profit % = (SP − CP)/CP × 100

**Shortcut Formula:** Actual weight = (Apparent SP)/(Real SP after profit)

**Common Trap:** Loss shown is fake; actual profit comes from less quantity.

**Exam Tip:** Always assume CP = 100 for easier percentage calculations.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the Mahar Movement in Maharashtra?

options.text: A socio-political movement for Dalit rights and social equality
A tribal uprising against British forest laws
A religious reform movement aimed at purifying Hindu rituals
A peasant movement against zamindari exploitation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A socio-political movement for Dalit rights and social equality**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mahar Movement** was a significant organized struggle in **Maharashtra** primarily led by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** in the early **20th century**. It was fundamentally a **socio-political movement** aimed at achieving **human rights**, **social equality**, and the destruction of the **caste system**. ***Hence, the first statement is correct.***
 
• A landmark event of this movement was the **Mahad Satyagraha** on **March 20, 1927**, where **Dr. Ambedkar** led the **Mahar community** to drink water from the **Chardar Tank** in **Mahad**, asserting their right to use public water resources.
 
• The movement also involved the symbolic **burning of the Manusmriti** in **December 1927**, representing a rejection of ancient texts that justified **untouchability** and social discrimination.
 
• The movement was not just social but also **political**, as it demanded **separate electorates** for the **Depressed Classes**, which eventually led to the **Poona Pact** of **1932**.
 
• Unlike **tribal uprisings** that fought against **British forest laws** or **peasant movements** against **landlords**, the Mahar movement focused on internal social reform and **constitutional safeguards** for the **Dalit** population. ***Hence, statements 2 and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:** The **Mahars** were a traditionally **untouchable** community in **Maharashtra** with a history of **military service** in the **British Indian Army** (notably the **Mahar Regiment**). This military background provided them with early exposure to **education** and **discipline**, fostering a sense of self-respect.
 
• **Early Pioneers:** Before **Dr. Ambedkar**, leaders like **Gopal Baba Walangkar** (who founded the **Anarya Dosha-Parihar Mandali** in **1888**) and **Shivram Janba Kamble** initiated efforts to organize the community and demand **government jobs**.
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj:** While **Jyotirao Phule**’s **Satyashodhak Samaj** (founded in **1873**) influenced the movement by critiquing **Brahmanical hegemony**, the Mahar movement under Ambedkar specifically transitioned from seeking **Sanskritization** (adopting upper-caste rituals) to **radical political mobilization**.
 
• **Contrast with Other Movements:**
 
 
• **Tribal Movements:** Examples include the **Santhal Rebellion (1855)** and **Munda Uprising (1899)**, which were primarily **anti-colonial** and **agrarian** in nature.
 
• **Peasant Movements:** Examples include the **Champaran Satyagraha (1917)** or the **Tebhaga Movement (1946)**, focusing on **rent reduction** and **land rights**.
 
• **Religious Reform:** Movements like the **Arya Samaj** aimed at **purifying rituals**, whereas the Mahar movement eventually moved away from **Hinduism** entirely.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conversion to Buddhism:** A major culmination of the movement occurred on **October 14, 1956**, at **Deekshabhoomi** in **Nagpur**, where **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** along with nearly **365,000** followers converted to **Buddhism** (Navayana), seeking a religious identity free from the **caste hierarchy**.
 
• **Education and Publication:** The movement utilized **journalism** as a tool, with publications like **Mooknayak (1920)** and **Bahishkrit Bharat (1927)** playing a pivotal role in **mass mobilization** and **public awareness**.
 
• **Impact on Modern India:** The Mahar movement laid the foundation for **Reservation Policy** in the **Indian Constitution** and continues to influence the **Dalit Panther** movement and modern **Ambedkarite** politics in **India**.

questions.question: Where did the Pune Book Festival 2025 take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fergusson College Grounds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pune Book Festival 2025** is organized at the **Fergusson College Grounds**, which is a prominent landmark located on **Fergusson College Road (FC Road)** in **Pune**, **Maharashtra**. This venue is historically significant and provides the vast open space required for such a large-scale literary gathering.
 
• The event is primarily organized by the **National Book Trust (NBT)**, an autonomous organization under the **Ministry of Education**, **Government of India**, in collaboration with the **Government of Maharashtra** and the **Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC)**.
 
• The main objective of the festival is to promote a **reading culture** and literature in various languages, including **Marathi**, **Hindi**, **English**, **Sanskrit**, and other regional Indian languages, aligning with the goals of the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**.
 
• The festival serves as a platform for **thousands of publishers** and booksellers to showcase millions of books, catering to all age groups, from children to senior citizens.
 
• The selection of **Fergusson College** as the venue is significant because the college itself is a symbol of the **Renaissance in Western India** and has been a hub for educational and cultural activities since its inception.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Book Trust (NBT), India:**

 
 
• It was established in the year **1957** by the Government of India.
 
• The **NBT** works under the **Department of Higher Education**, **Ministry of Education**.
 
• Its primary mandate is to produce and encourage the production of good literature and to make such literature available at moderate prices to the public.
 
 
 
• **Fergusson College:**
 
 
• Founded in **1885** by the **Deccan Education Society (DES)**.
 
• It was named after **Sir James Fergusson**, the then Governor of Bombay.
 
• Founding members included legendary figures such as **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, **Gopal Ganesh Agarkar**, and **Mahadev Ballal Namjoshi**.
 
 
 
• **Pune's Literary Heritage:**
 
 
• **Pune** is widely recognized as the **'Cultural Capital of Maharashtra'** and the **'Oxford of the East'** due to its high density of educational institutions and literary history.
 
• The city hosts various other literary events like the **Pune International Literary Festival (PILF)** and several **Marathi Sahitya Sammelans**.
 
 
 
• **Guinness World Records:**
 
 
• During the **2023** edition of the **Pune Book Festival**, the city set a **Guinness World Record** for the **'Largest Reading Activity'**, where **3,066** parents read to their children simultaneously, surpassing the previous record held by China.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Pune Book Festival** typically includes a **'Bal Sahitya Melawa'** (Children's Literature Festival) to engage young readers through storytelling, workshops, and interactive sessions.
 
• The venue, **Fergusson College Grounds**, allows for the setup of hundreds of stalls, separate stages for literary discussions, and dedicated zones for food and cultural performances.
 
• The festival reflects **India's G20 Presidency** themes of **'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'** (The World is One Family) by showcasing books that promote global knowledge and Indian heritage.
 
• It also emphasizes **digital literacy** by featuring sections on **e-books** and digital libraries alongside traditional printed media.

questions.question: How many main approaches are there to human development?

options.text: Six: income, welfare, basic needs, capabilities, rights-based, participatory approaches
Five: income, welfare, capabilities, rights-based, and sustainability approaches
Three: income, welfare, and capability approaches
Four: income, welfare, minimum needs, and capabilities approaches

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four: income, welfare, minimum needs, and capabilities approaches**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Income Approach** is one of the **oldest** methods used to measure human development. It links the level of development directly to **income**, under the assumption that higher income reflects a higher level of human development and greater freedom. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect as it includes participatory and rights-based approaches which are not part of the four "main" traditional classifications.***
 
• The **Welfare Approach** views human beings as **beneficiaries** or targets of all development activities. This approach argues for higher government **expenditure** on **education**, **health**, and other social sectors to improve the quality of life. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Basic Needs Approach** was initially proposed by the **International Labour Organisation (ILO)**. It identifies **six** basic needs: **health**, **education**, **food**, **water supply**, **sanitation**, and **housing**. This approach ignores the question of human choices and focuses primarily on the provision of these necessities. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Capability Approach** is closely associated with the work of **Prof. Amartya Sen**, the **Indian Nobel Laureate**. It focuses on building human **capabilities** in the areas of health, education, and access to **resources** as the key to increasing human development. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Collectively, these **four** methods represent the primary framework through which human development has been historically analyzed and implemented by global organizations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concept of Human Development:** The concept was introduced by **Dr. Mahbub ul Haq**, a **Pakistani** economist, in **1990**. He described it as development that enlarges people's **choices** and improves their lives.
 
• **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP):** Since **1990**, the **UNDP** has published the **Human Development Report (HDR)** annually. This report provides the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, which ranks countries based on their progress in key dimensions.
 
• **Dimensions of HDI:** The index is a composite statistic of **life expectancy** (Health), **education** (Mean years of schooling and Expected years of schooling), and **per capita income** (Standard of living) indicators.
 
• **Amartya Sen’s Contribution:** **Prof. Amartya Sen** emphasized that the objective of development is to increase **freedom**. He argued that the lack of **capabilities** (like illiteracy or poor health) limits the choices people can make, thereby hindering development.
 
• **Global Trends:** Modern reports, such as the **2023-24 HDR**, now also consider factors like **planetary pressures** and **inequality** (IHDI) to provide a more holistic view of global progress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Linguistic and Cultural Factors:** While not part of the "four main approaches," factors like **gender empowerment** and **political freedom** are often measured through supplementary indices like the **Gender Inequality Index (GII)**.
 
• **Income vs. Capability:** A crucial distinction in these approaches is that while the **Income Approach** focuses on what people **have**, the **Capability Approach** focuses on what people are **capable of doing** with what they have.
 
• **Government Policy:** The **Welfare Approach** is often the basis for **Social Security** programs and **Universal Healthcare** initiatives in many countries, including **India**.
 
• **ILO Standards:** The **Basic Needs Approach** remains relevant for **developing nations** striving to meet the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** set by the **United Nations** for **2030**.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of application software that depends entirely on system software to function?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Microsoft Word**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Microsoft Word** is a prime example of **Application Software**. This type of software is designed to perform specific tasks for the end-user, such as **word processing**, document creation, and formatting.
 
• Application software like **Microsoft Word** depends entirely on **System Software** (the **Operating System**) to function because it cannot interact directly with the computer's **Hardware** (such as the **CPU**, **RAM**, or **Hard Drive**). ***Hence, the option Microsoft Word is the correct answer.***
 
• **BIOS** (Basic Input/Output System) is a type of **Firmware** and **System Software** that initializes hardware during the **Booting** process. It does not depend on other system software to start; rather, it is the first software to run when a computer is powered on. ***Hence, the statement regarding BIOS as an application software is incorrect.***
 
• **Ubuntu** is a popular **Linux-based Operating System**. It is categorized as **System Software** because its primary function is to manage computer resources and provide a platform for application programs. ***Hence, the statement regarding Ubuntu being an application software is incorrect.***
 
• The **Linux Kernel** is the core component of the **Linux Operating System**. It acts as a bridge between **Software** and **Hardware**. It is the most fundamental part of **System Software** and manages low-level tasks like **Memory Management** and **Process Scheduling**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Linux Kernel being an application software is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Application Software**:

 
 
• These are programs developed to assist users in performing specific personal, educational, or business tasks.
 
• **Functions**: Includes **Data Manipulation**, **Image Editing**, **Web Browsing**, and **Communication**.
 
• **Examples**: **Google Chrome** (Web Browser), **Adobe Photoshop** (Graphics Editor), **VLC Media Player**, and **Microsoft Excel** (Spreadsheet).
 
• **Characteristics**: They are usually written in **High-Level Languages** like **Java**, **C++**, or **Python** and require an **Operating System** to execute their instructions.
 
 
 
• **System Software**:
 
 
• This software acts as an interface between the user, the application software, and the computer's hardware.
 
• **Categories**: It includes **Operating Systems** (like **Windows 11**, **macOS**, and **Android**), **Language Translators** (Compilers and Interpreters), and **Device Drivers**.
 
• **Utility Software**: A sub-category of system software used for maintenance, such as **Antivirus** software, **Disk Defragmenters**, and **Compression** tools (like **WinZip**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dependency Layer**: In a computing environment, the hierarchy of operation starts with the **Hardware** at the bottom, followed by the **System Software** (OS), then the **Application Software**, and finally the **User** at the top.
 
• **Interaction**: When a user types a character in **Microsoft Word**, the application sends a request to the **Operating System**, which then instructs the **Hardware** (Keyboard and Monitor) to process and display the input.
 
• **Installation**: **System Software** is typically installed when the computer is set up, whereas **Application Software** is installed by the user based on their specific needs.
 
• **Execution**: **System Software** starts running as soon as the computer is turned on and stays active until the system is shut down, whereas **Application Software** only runs when triggered by the user.

questions.question:
Find the value of m, satisfying equation:

((28)/(9))¹¹ times ((9)/(28))¹⁶ times ((28)/(9))¹⁷ = ((9)/(28))²m ⁺ ⁸
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Convert everything into same base: (28/9) and (9/28)

⇒ (9/28) = (28/9)−¹

⇒ Total power of (28/9) = 11 + 17 − 16 = 12

⇒ RHS: (9/28)²m⁺⁸ = (28/9)−⁽²m⁺⁸⁾

questions.question: Choose the correct statement regarding the process of photosynthesis in plants.

options.text: It occurs in the mitochondria of plant cells.
It converts light energy into chemical energy.
It involves the breakdown of glucose to produce energy.
It primarily takes place during the night to conserve water.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It converts light energy into chemical energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Photosynthesis** is the biological process by which **green plants**, **algae**, and certain **bacteria** transform **light energy** into **chemical energy**. This energy is stored in the **bonds of sugar** (glucose).
 
• It occurs in the **chloroplasts** of plant cells, specifically within the **thylakoid membranes** and the **stroma**, not in the **mitochondria**. Mitochondria are primarily responsible for **cellular respiration**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The core **function** of this process is the conversion of **solar radiation** into stable **chemical energy**. This process supports almost all life on **Earth** by providing the primary **energy source** in the **food chain**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The process involves the **synthesis of glucose** from **carbon dioxide** and **water**, rather than the breakdown of glucose. The **breakdown of glucose** to release **ATP** is a characteristic of **respiration**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Photosynthesis consists of **light-dependent reactions** which require **direct sunlight** to split **water molecules**. While the **light-independent reactions** (Calvin Cycle) can occur without light, they rely on **ATP** and **NADPH** produced during the day. It does not primarily take place at **night**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chlorophyll**: This is the primary **pigment** involved in photosynthesis. It is located in the **chloroplast** and is responsible for absorbing **blue** and **red** light while reflecting **green** light, which gives plants their **color**.
 
• **The Chemical Equation**: The generalized **balanced equation** for photosynthesis is **6CO2 + 6H2O + Light Energy → C6H12O6 + 6O2**. This shows that **six molecules** of carbon dioxide and **six molecules** of water are converted into **one molecule** of glucose and **six molecules** of oxygen.
 
• **Stomata**: These are **microscopic pores** located on the **epidermis** of leaves. Their primary **function** is to allow the **entry of CO2** and the **exit of O2** and **water vapor** through **transpiration**.
 
• **Organisms**: While **terrestrial plants** are the most visible photosynthesizers, **phytoplankton** in the **oceans** contribute to nearly **50%** of the **oxygen** produced on **Earth**.
 
• **History**: The **discovery** of photosynthesis evolved over **centuries**, with significant **data** contributed by **Jan Ingenhousz** in **1779**, who demonstrated that **light** is necessary for plants to **purify air**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Light-Dependent Reaction**: This stage takes place in the **grana** of the chloroplast. It involves **photolysis of water**, where water is split into **oxygen**, **protons**, and **electrons**.
 
• **Calvin Cycle (C3 Cycle)**: Named after **Melvin Calvin**, who won the **Nobel Prize** in **1961**. This stage occurs in the **stroma** and utilizes **CO2** to produce **sugar**.
 
• **Limiting Factors**: The **rate** of photosynthesis is influenced by **factors** such as **light intensity**, **carbon dioxide concentration**, and **temperature** (optimally between **25°C to 35°C** for many species).
 
• **C4 and CAM Pathways**: Certain plants in **arid locations** have evolved **specialized features** to minimize **photorespiration** and **water loss**, such as **Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM)** where **CO2** is taken up at **night**.
 
• **Applications**: Understanding photosynthesis is crucial for **agriculture**, **forestry**, and developing **artificial photosynthesis** technologies to produce **clean fuels** like **hydrogen**.

questions.question: Which material was mainly used for making beads and seals in Harappan civilization?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steatite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Steatite**, also commonly referred to as **soapstone**, was the primary material utilized by the craftsmen of the **Harappan Civilization** (also known as the **Indus Valley Civilization**) for the production of **seals** and **beads**.
 
• The choice of **steatite** was largely due to its physical properties; it is a **soft mineral** (composed mainly of **talc**) that is exceptionally easy to carve into intricate designs and scripts using **copper tools**.
 
• Once the carving process was complete, the **Harappan** artisans would often apply a **whitening paste** or silica coating to the **steatite** and then **fire** it in a kiln. This heating process caused the stone to harden significantly, giving it a durable, white, and lustrous finish.
 
• The **Harappan seals** were typically **square** or **rectangular** in shape, with dimensions often around **2x2 centimeters** or **5x5 centimeters**. These seals usually featured an **animal motif** (such as the **unicorn**, **bull**, **elephant**, or **tiger**) and a short inscription in the **Indus script**.
 
• In the context of **bead-making**, **steatite** was used to create a variety of shapes, including **disc**, **cylindrical**, and **spherical** forms. The civilization is particularly noted for its **micro-beads** made of **steatite**, which required high levels of technical precision.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of Seals:** The **seals** served as vital tools for **long-distance trade**. They were used to stamp **clay tags** on bundles of goods. If the impression remained intact upon reaching its destination, it served as proof that the package had not been tampered with and authenticated the identity of the **sender**.
 
• **Diverse Materials:** While **steatite** was the most common, other materials used for making beads and seals included **terracotta** (fired clay), **faience** (a glazed ceramic material), **agate**, **chert**, **carnelian**, **jasper**, **copper**, **gold**, and **ivory**.
 
• **Manufacturing Centers:** Archeological excavations have identified specific industrial hubs for bead and seal production. **Chanhudaro** and **Lothal** (in present-day **Gujarat**) were renowned centers for **bead-making**, featuring specialized **drills** and workshops.
 
• **The Pashupati Seal:** One of the most famous **steatite** artifacts is the **Pashupati Seal** found at **Mohenjo-daro**. It depicts a figure sitting in a **yogic posture**, surrounded by animals like a **rhino**, **buffalo**, **elephant**, and **tiger**, providing insights into the religious beliefs of the period.
 
• **Indus Script:** Most **steatite** seals carry inscriptions in the **Indus script**, which remains **undeciphered** to this day. The script is usually written from **right to left** (boustrophedon style).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chronology:** The **Harappan Civilization** flourished during the **Bronze Age**, primarily between **2600 BCE and 1900 BCE** (the **Mature Harappan phase**).
 
• **Geographical Extent:** The civilization covered a vast area including modern-day **Pakistan**, **Northwest India** (states like **Rajasthan**, **Gujarat**, **Haryana**, and **Punjab**), and parts of **Afghanistan**.
 
• **Bead Varieties:** The **Harappans** were masters of **lapidary** work. For instance, **carnelian** (a beautiful red stone) was sourced from **Bharuch** in **Gujarat** to make highly prized beads.
 
• **Standardization:** The production of **steatite seals** shows a high degree of **standardization** in weight and measure across different cities like **Harappa**, **Mohenjo-daro**, and **Kalibangan**, indicating a centralized or highly organized administrative system.
 
• **Artistic Legacy:** The use of **steatite** allowed for **realistic carvings** of animals, which are considered some of the finest examples of **proto-historic art** in the world.

questions.question: According to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, which of the following states was the major groundnut exporting state of India in 2020-2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gujarat** emerged as the leading state in groundnut production and exports in **India** during the financial year **2020-2021**. The state consistently accounts for a massive share, often exceeding **40%**, of the total groundnut production in the country.
 
• The **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, through its nodal agency **APEDA** (Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority), reported that **India** exported a total of **6.38 lakh metric tonnes** of groundnuts worth **USD 727 million** (approximately **Rs. 5,381 crores**) during **2020-21**.
 
• The major groundnut-producing regions in **Gujarat** are concentrated in the **Saurashtra** belt, including districts like **Junagadh**, **Rajkot**, **Amreli**, and **Bhavnagar**. The presence of **well-drained sandy loam soil** in these areas makes it ideal for cultivation.
 
• During the year **2020-2021**, despite the global pandemic, **Gujarat** maintained its dominance due to its robust **supply chain infrastructure** and proximity to major ports like **Kandla** and **Mudra**, which facilitate easy **international trade**.
 
• The state’s success is attributed to the adoption of **high-yielding varieties** and **modern irrigation techniques**, which have significantly improved the **productivity** per hectare compared to other states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Groundnut Characteristics and Uses:**

 
 
• Groundnut (**Arachis hypogaea**) is a unique crop as it is a **legume** that matures its fruit underground. It is a rich source of **protein** (approx **25%**), **edible oil** (**48-50%**), and **vitamins**.
 
• In **India**, it is primarily grown as a **Kharif crop** (sown in **June-July** and harvested in **October-November**), but in states like **Tamil Nadu** and **Andhra Pradesh**, it is also grown as a **Rabi crop**.
 
• The **uses** of groundnut range from direct human consumption (as **table nuts**), extraction of **peanut oil** for cooking, and the manufacture of **peanut butter** and **confectionery products**.
 
 
 
• **Global and National Standing:**
 
 
• **India** is the **second-largest producer** of groundnuts in the **world**, following **China**.
 
• The major **export destinations** for Indian groundnuts in **2020-21** included **Indonesia**, **Vietnam**, **Philippines**, **Thailand**, and **Malaysia**.
 
• Other significant groundnut-producing states in **India** include **Rajasthan**, **Tamil Nadu**, **Andhra Pradesh**, and **Karnataka**, but **Gujarat** remains the undisputed leader in **export volume**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Export Varieties:** The two main varieties of groundnuts exported from **India** are **Bold** and **Java**. The **Java** variety is smaller and rounder, while the **Bold** variety is larger and elongated.
 
• **Quality Control:** To maintain its status as a **major exporter**, **India** follows strict guidelines regarding **Aflatoxin** levels. **APEDA** has established **monitoring laboratories** to ensure that the produce meets **European Union** and **South East Asian** safety standards.
 
• **Climate Requirements:** The crop requires a **temperature** between **20°C and 30°C** and a moderate **rainfall** of **50 cm to 100 cm**. Excessive rain during the ripening stage can damage the **pods**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** In **2020-2021**, the groundnut sector provided significant **employment** to millions of farmers in **Gujarat** and contributed substantially to the **foreign exchange reserves** of **India**.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts provides statutory status to Lok Adalats in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lok Adalat** (People's Court) is one of the **Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)** mechanisms in India, which serves as a forum where disputes or cases pending in the court of law or at the pre-litigation stage are settled or compromised amicably.
 
• **Lok Adalats** have been given **statutory status** under the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**. This specific legislation provides a legal framework for the organization and functioning of these forums across the **country**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 is correct.***
 
• Under this **Act**, the award (decision) made by the **Lok Adalats** is deemed to be a **decree of a civil court** and is **final and binding** on all parties involved. No appeal lies to any court against such an award.
 
• The primary objective of this **Act** is to fulfill the mandate of **Article 39A** of the **Constitution of India**, which directs the **State** to provide **free legal aid** to the weaker sections of society and ensure **justice for all**.
 
• The organization of **Lok Adalats** is handled by the **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)** along with other legal services institutions at the **State, District, and Taluk levels**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Indian Constitution**: While the **Constitution** contains **Article 39A** (inserted by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**) which provides the philosophical basis for **legal aid**, it is not the specific **Act** that provides the operational statutory status to **Lok Adalats**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996**: This **legislation** primarily deals with **domestic arbitration**, **international commercial arbitration**, and **conciliation**. While it is a part of the **ADR** family, it does not govern the **Lok Adalat** system. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **The Civil Procedure Code (CPC), 1908**: **Section 89** of the **CPC** was amended to allow courts to refer pending cases to **ADR** methods like **mediation** and **Lok Adalats** to reduce the burden on the judiciary. However, the **CPC** itself is not the source of statutory status for **Lok Adalats**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Historical Context**: The first **Lok Adalat** in post-independence India was held on **March 14, 1982**, at **Junagadh** in **Gujarat**. It was a voluntary and conciliatory agency without any **statutory** backing at that time, before the **1987 Act** was implemented.
 
• **Benefits**: One of the major **features** of **Lok Adalats** is that there is **no court fee**. If a case already filed in a regular court is settled in a **Lok Adalat**, the **fee** paid to the court is **refunded** to the parties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Composition**: A **Lok Adalat** generally consists of a **judicial officer** (sitting or retired) as the chairman, along with two other members, usually a **lawyer** and a **social worker**.
 
• **Jurisdiction**: They can deal with **civil cases**, **matrimonial disputes**, **land acquisition** cases, **labour disputes**, **compoundable criminal offences**, and **bank recovery cases**.
 
• **Permanent Lok Adalats**: The **Legal Services Authorities Act** was amended in **2002** to provide for the establishment of **Permanent Lok Adalats** to deal with **Public Utility Services** such as **transport**, **postal**, **telegraph**, **power**, and **water supply**. Unlike regular **Lok Adalats**, **Permanent Lok Adalats** have the power to decide a case on **merits** even if the parties fail to reach a **compromise**.
 
• **National Lok Adalats**: These are held on a **single day** throughout the **country** in all courts from the **Supreme Court** to the **Taluk levels** at regular intervals to dispose of a massive **number** of cases.

questions.question: Under the Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS), exporters are rewarded in the form of:

options.text: Export tax rebates that expire on use

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Freely transferable Duty Credit Scrips**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS)** was introduced in the **Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2015-20**. It aimed to provide financial **incentives** to exporters to offset infrastructural inefficiencies and associated costs involved in exporting goods manufactured or produced in India.
 
• Under this scheme, exporters are rewarded in the form of **Duty Credit Scrips**. These scrips are a type of certificate that allows the holder to pay various **customs duties** using the credit balance instead of cash.
 
• A defining **feature** of these scrips is that they are **freely transferable**. This means an exporter who receives a scrip but does not need to import any goods can sell the scrip in the open market to another importer at a **discounted rate**. ***Hence, the statement regarding freely transferable duty credit scrips is correct.***
 
• The value of the reward is calculated as a percentage (typically **2%, 3%, or 5%**) of the **Free on Board (FOB)** value of the exported goods in **free foreign exchange**.
 
• The scheme merged five earlier incentive programs, including the **Focus Product Scheme (FPS)** and the **Focus Market Scheme (FMS)**, into a single, streamlined program to simplify the export process.
 
• The rewards are not provided in the form of **equity shares**, as the scheme is designed for immediate fiscal relief rather than long-term capital investment in **Export Oriented Units (EOUs)**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The scrips are **transferable** and are not **cash vouchers**, which differentiates them from direct cash subsidies. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While the scrips are used to offset taxes, they are specifically **tradable instruments** rather than just rebates that expire on a single use by the original exporter. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transition to RoDTEP:** Due to challenges at the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**, where **MEIS** was viewed as a prohibited export subsidy, the **Government of India** replaced it with the **Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP)** scheme. This transition took effect from **January 1, 2021**.
 
• **Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT):** The **DGFT**, under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, is the primary body responsible for formulating the **Foreign Trade Policy** and issuing **Duty Credit Scrips** to eligible exporters.
 
• **Utilization of Scrips:** These scrips can be used for the payment of **Basic Customs Duty (BCD)** on imports of inputs or goods, including capital goods. However, they generally cannot be used to pay **Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST)** or **Compensation Cess** under the **GST** regime.
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:** The scheme covers a vast range of products, including **agricultural goods**, **textiles**, **electronics**, and **pharmaceuticals**. Exporters must have an **IEC (Importer Exporter Code)** and must submit their claims online through the **DGFT portal** within a specified **time limit** from the date of export.
 
• **Market Categorization:** Initially, **MEIS** categorized global markets into three groups (**Group A, B, and C**) to determine the level of incentive, with higher rewards often provided for exports to markets with higher **logistics costs** or strategic importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **WTO Compliance:** The shift from **MEIS** to **RoDTEP** was necessary because **RoDTEP** is a **tax-neutral** scheme that refunds internal taxes (like electricity duty or fuel tax) that were previously not refunded, making it **WTO-compliant**.

questions.question: Sharad is two times as old as his younger brother, and his other brother is 3 years younger than the younger brother. If the sum of the ages of these three brothers 3 years ago was 28 years, find Sharad’s present age, in years.

• **Windows Media Audio (WMA)** is a proprietary **audio data compression technology** developed by **Microsoft**. It is both an audio codec and its corresponding audio format.
 
• The **.wma** file extension is used to identify these audio files, which are part of the broader **Windows Media framework**.
 
• The format was first released in **1999** by **Microsoft** as a competitor to the widely popular **MP3** and **RealAudio** formats, claiming to offer better compression efficiency.
 
• **Wired Media Audio format** is a non-existent technical term in computer science and does not correspond to any standard file extension. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Windows Media Audio format** is the correct expansion for the **.wma** extension, representing the suite of audio codecs developed for the **Windows** ecosystem. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***
 
• **Wireless Media Audio format** refers generally to audio transmitted over wireless protocols (like Bluetooth or RF), but it is not a specific file format name. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **WiFi Media Audio format** refers to networking standards (IEEE 802.11) used for data transfer, but there is no such audio file format under this name. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

• **Container Format:** A **.wma** file is typically encapsulated in the **Advanced Systems Format (ASF)** container, which is a proprietary **Microsoft** container for digital audio and video streams.
 
• **Digital Rights Management (DRM):** One of the significant features of the **WMA** format is its support for **DRM**. This allows content providers to protect their music from unauthorized copying or playback on non-licensed devices.
 
• **Compatibility:** While natively supported on **Windows** via **Windows Media Player**, users on **macOS** or **Linux** often require third-party software like **VLC Media Player** or specific codecs to play these files.
 
• **Compression Algorithm:** It uses a **lossy compression** method (except for the Lossless version) that removes certain parts of the audio data that the human ear cannot easily perceive to reduce **file size**.

• **Licensing:** Unlike the **MP3** format, which became royalty-free in **2017**, **WMA** remains a proprietary technology owned by **Microsoft Corporation**.
 
• **Device Support:** Many hardware portable media players and car stereos from the early **2000s** and **2010s** were marketed with "WMA Support" as a key feature alongside **MP3** compatibility.

questions.question: Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden performed the famous α–particle scattering experiment under the supervision of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ernest Rutherford**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ernest Rutherford**, a **New Zealand**-born physicist, is credited with the discovery of the atomic nucleus. He supervised the **alpha-particle scattering experiment**, also known as the **Gold Foil Experiment**, which was performed by his students **Hans Geiger** and **Ernest Marsden** in **1909**.
 
• In this experiment, high-energy **alpha particles** (doubly charged **helium ions** with a mass of **4u**) were directed at a very thin **gold foil**, which was approximately **1000 atoms thick**. This was done to observe how the particles interacted with the matter inside the gold atoms.
 
• Rutherford observed that most of the alpha particles passed straight through the **gold foil** without any deflection. This led to the conclusion that most of the space inside an **atom** is empty. ***Hence, the experiment fundamentally changed the understanding of atomic structure.***
 
• A small fraction of particles were deflected by small angles, and about **1 in 12,000** particles rebounded almost **180 degrees** back. This indicated that the **positive charge** and nearly all the **mass** of the atom were concentrated in a very small, dense region called the **nucleus**.
 
• Based on these observations, **Ernest Rutherford** proposed the **Nuclear Model of an Atom**, which states that an atom has a **positively charged center** where the **electrons** revolve around it in circular paths.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **John Dalton:** He was an **English** chemist and physicist who proposed the first modern **Atomic Theory** in **1803**. He suggested that atoms were **indivisible** and **indestructible** spheres. However, Rutherford's experiment later proved that atoms are divisible and consist of subatomic particles.
 
• **Niels Bohr:** A **Danish** physicist who improved upon Rutherford’s model in **1913**. **Bohr** postulated that **electrons** move in specific **discrete orbits** or **energy levels** around the nucleus without radiating energy, thus addressing the stability issues in Rutherford's model.
 
• **William Henry:** He was an **English** chemist known for **Henry's Law**, which relates the amount of gas dissolved in a liquid to its partial pressure. He did not play a direct role in the discovery of the atomic nucleus or the **scattering experiment**.
 
• **Alpha Particles:** These are **positively charged** particles consisting of **two protons** and **two neutrons**. They are identical to the nucleus of a **helium-4** atom. Because of their **positive charge**, they were repelled by the **nucleus** during the experiment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The experiment utilized a **Zinc Sulfide (ZnS)** screen placed around the **gold foil**. When an alpha particle struck the screen, it produced a tiny flash of light, allowing the researchers to track the **location** and **angle** of the particles after they passed through or hit the foil.
 
• The **radius** of the **nucleus** was calculated to be about **10 to the power of 5** times smaller than the **radius** of the **atom**. If an atom were the size of a **football stadium**, the nucleus would be about the size of a **small marble** in the center.
 
• **Ernest Rutherford** received the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry** in **1908** for his investigations into the disintegration of elements and the chemistry of **radioactive substances**.
 
• This experiment famously disproved **J.J. Thomson’s Plum Pudding Model**, which suggested that **positive charge** was spread uniformly throughout the atom like a pudding with **electrons** embedded like plums.

questions.question: The monthly incomes of two friends Vipul and Vijay, are in the ratio 6 : 7 respectively and each of them saves ₹66,000 every month. If the ratio of their monthly expenditure is 1 : 3, find the monthly income of Vipul (in ₹).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Income ratio = 6 : 7, Expenditure ratio = 1 : 3

⇒ Saving same ⇒ Difference between income and expenditure equal

⇒ Take income = 6x, 7x and expenditure = y, 3y

⇒ 6x − y = 7x − 3y

⇒ x = 2y

⇒ Saving = 6x − y = 66000

⇒ 6(2y) − y = 66000 ⇒ 11y = 66000 ⇒ y = 6000

⇒ x = 12000

⇒ Vipul income = 6x = 72000

**∴ Answer = 72000**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income ratio = 6 : 7

Expenditure ratio = 1 : 3

Savings of each = 66000

**Concept Used:**

Income − Expenditure = Savings

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let incomes be 6x and 7x

⇒ Let expenditures be y and 3y

⇒ For Vipul: 6x − y = 66000

⇒ For Vijay: 7x − 3y = 66000

⇒ 6x − y = 7x − 3y

⇒ x = 2y

⇒ Substitute in first equation:

⇒ 6(2y) − y = 66000

⇒ 12y − y = 66000

⇒ 11y = 66000

⇒ y = 6000

⇒ x = 2y = 12000

⇒ Vipul income = 6x = 72000

**∴ The correct answer is 72000.**

questions.question: According to the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023, what proportion of seats to be filled by direct election in the House of the People (Lok Sabha) is to be reserved for women?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-third of the seats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023**, popularly known as the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**, seeks to reserve **one-third** (approximately **33%**) of all seats for women in the **Lok Sabha** (House of the People) and the **State Legislative Assemblies**.
 
• The bill for this amendment was introduced as the **Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2023**, in the **Lok Sabha** on **September 19, 2023**, during a special session of **Parliament** held in the new Parliament building.
 
• The Act mandates that **one-third** of the total number of seats filled by **direct election** in the **Lok Sabha** shall be reserved for women. This includes seats reserved for women within the existing quotas for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**.
 
• The reservation will also apply to the **Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi**. The implementation of this reservation is contingent upon the conduct of a **Census** and the subsequent **delimitation** exercise (readjustment of constituencies) based on that census data.
 
• This historic legislation received the **President's assent** on **September 28, 2023**, marking a significant milestone in India's legislative history regarding **gender representation** and **women's empowerment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Articles Inserted:** The amendment introduced new articles into the **Constitution of India**, including **Article 330A** (for Lok Sabha reservation), **Article 332A** (for State Assemblies), and **Article 334A** (regarding the sunset clause).
 
• **Duration and Sunset Clause:** The reservation is initially set for a period of **15 years** from the date of its commencement. However, the **Parliament** has the authority to extend this period by enacting further laws if deemed necessary.
 
• **Rotation of Seats:** The Act provides that the seats reserved for women shall be **rotated** to different constituencies in the **State** or **Union Territory** after every subsequent exercise of **delimitation**.
 
• **Scope of the Act:** It is important to note that this reservation does not apply to the **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States) or the **State Legislative Councils** (Upper Houses of State Legislatures), where members are not **directly elected** by the people.
 
• **Historical Context:** The quest for women's reservation in the Indian **Parliament** dates back several decades, with earlier versions of the bill being introduced in **1996, 1998, 1999, and 2008**, but failing to pass both houses until the **2023** amendment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Delimitation Condition:** **Article 334A** specifies that the reservation will come into effect only after an exercise of **delimitation** is undertaken following the publication of the relevant figures of the first **Census** conducted after the **Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023** comes into force.
 
• **Voting Statistics:** The bill was passed almost unanimously in the **Lok Sabha** with **454 votes** in favor and only **2 against**. In the **Rajya Sabha**, it was passed **unanimously** with **214 votes** on **September 21, 2023**.
 
• **Union Law Minister:** The bill was moved in the **Parliament** by the **Union Minister of Law and Justice**, **Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal**.
 
• **Impact on Total Seats:** In the current **Lok Sabha** with **543 seats**, once implemented, the number of women members will rise to at least **181**, significantly increasing from the **82** women members elected in the **2019** general elections.

questions.question: What is the process by which plants make their food using sunlight?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Photosynthesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Photosynthesis** is the fundamental **biological process** by which **autotrophic organisms**, such as **green plants**, **algae**, and certain **cyanobacteria**, synthesize their own food. This process effectively converts **solar energy** into **chemical energy** stored in the bonds of **carbohydrates**.
 
• The process primarily takes place in the **leaves** of the plant, specifically within specialized organelles called **chloroplasts**. These organelles contain the pigment **chlorophyll**, which is responsible for capturing **light energy** from the sun.
 
• For **Photosynthesis** to occur, the plant requires three essential raw materials: **Carbon dioxide (CO2)** absorbed from the **atmosphere** through the **stomata**, **Water (H2O)** absorbed from the **soil** via the **roots**, and **Sunlight**.
 
• The primary product of this reaction is **Glucose (C6H12O6)**, a simple **sugar** that serves as the main source of energy for the plant's **growth** and **metabolism**. A vital byproduct of this process is **Oxygen (O2)**, which is released back into the air.
 
• The generalized **chemical equation** for the process is: **6CO2 + 6H2O + Light Energy -> C6H12O6 + 6O2**. ***Hence, Photosynthesis is the correct process described in the question.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Respiration:**

 
 
• Unlike photosynthesis, **respiration** is a **catabolic process** that occurs in all living cells, including plants. It involves the breakdown of **glucose** in the presence of **oxygen** to release energy in the form of **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**.
 
• This process takes place in the **mitochondria** and produces **carbon dioxide** and **water** as waste products. While photosynthesis "builds" food, respiration "burns" it for energy. ***Hence, statement regarding respiration is incorrect in the context of food making.***
 
 
 
• **Transpiration:**
 
 
• **Transpiration** is the **evaporation** of water from the **aerial parts** of a plant, mainly through the **stomata** on the **leaves**.
 
• This process creates a **suction force** (transpiration pull) that helps in the **upward movement** of **water** and **minerals** from the roots to the rest of the plant. It also helps in **cooling** the plant during hot weather. ***Hence, statement regarding transpiration is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Fermentation:**
 
 
• **Fermentation** is an **anaerobic** (occurring without oxygen) metabolic process. It is used by **microorganisms** like **yeast** and **bacteria** to convert **sugars** into **ethanol**, **lactic acid**, or **gases**.
 
• In humans, it occurs in **muscle cells** during intense exercise when oxygen supply is low, leading to the production of **lactic acid**. It is not a method for plants to manufacture food using sunlight. ***Hence, statement regarding fermentation is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Two Stages of Photosynthesis:** The process is divided into the **Light-dependent reactions**, which occur in the **thylakoid membranes** of the chloroplasts, and the **Light-independent reactions** (also known as the **Calvin Cycle**), which take place in the **stroma**.
 
• **Factors Affecting the Rate:** The efficiency of food production in plants is influenced by several external factors:
 
 
• **Light Intensity:** Increasing light generally increases the rate up to a certain point.
 
• **Temperature:** Enzymes required for the process work best within a specific **temperature range** (usually **25°C to 35°C**).
 
• **CO2 Concentration:** Since **carbon dioxide** is a raw material, its availability directly affects the speed of the reaction.
 
 
 
• **Global Significance:** Photosynthesis is the primary source of all **organic matter** on **Earth**. It is responsible for maintaining the **Oxygen levels** in the atmosphere (approximately **21%**), which is essential for the **survival** of aerobic organisms.
 
• **Vascular Tissues:** The **Xylem** tissue is responsible for transporting **water** from the roots to the leaves for photosynthesis, while the **Phloem** tissue transports the manufactured **glucose** (food) to other parts of the plant.

questions.question: Which Classical Language underwent significant scriptural evolution from Grantha, Vatteluttu, Kolezhuthu, and finally to its current script used in modern writing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malayalam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Malayalam** is a **Dravidian language** primarily spoken in the Indian state of **Kerala** and the union territories of **Lakshadweep** and **Puducherry**. It underwent a complex scriptural evolution involving **Vatteluttu**, **Grantha**, and **Kolezhuthu**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the scriptural evolution refers to Malayalam and is correct.***
 
• The earliest script used for **Malayalam** was **Vatteluttu** (meaning "round writing"), which was also used for **Tamil**. By the **9th century AD**, as seen in the **Vazhappally Inscription** (dated **830 AD**), **Vatteluttu** was the dominant script for the region.
 
• The **Grantha** script was later introduced to represent **Sanskrit** phonemes that were not present in the **Vatteluttu** alphabet. This led to a hybrid script known as **Arya Ezhuthu**, which eventually evolved into the modern **Malayalam** script.
 
• **Kolezhuthu** (meaning "rod-writing") was a derivative of **Vatteluttu** used primarily for maintaining land records and administrative documents in the **Malabar** and **Cochin** regions until the **18th century**.
 
• **Malayalam** was officially designated as a **Classical Language** of India in **May 2013**, becoming the **fifth** language to receive this status. This recognition was based on its high antiquity, a body of ancient literature, and an original literary tradition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tamil**: It was the **first** language to be declared a **Classical Language** in **2004**. Its script evolved from **Tamil Brahmi** to **Vatteluttu** and finally to the modern **Tamil** script. It is primarily spoken in **Tamil Nadu** and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• **Sanskrit**: Declared a **Classical Language** in **2005**. It is the liturgical language of **Hinduism** and has a vast body of literature including the **Vedas** and **Upanishads**. Its modern script is **Devanagari**.
 
• **Kannada and Telugu**: Both were granted **Classical Language** status in **2008**. **Kannada** script evolved from the **Kadamba** script, while **Telugu** shares a common scriptural ancestor (**Old Kannada-Telugu script**) with **Kannada**.
 
• **Odia**: It was declared a **Classical Language** in **2014**. The **Odia** script is a descendant of the **Brahmi** script and is used in the state of **Odisha**. It is known for its unique curved appearance due to the historical practice of writing on palm leaves.
 
• The **Ministry of Culture** sets the criteria for **Classical Languages**, which includes a recorded history of over **1500-2000 years** and a literary heritage that is considered valuable by generations of speakers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Thunchaththu Ezhuthachan**, a **16th-century** poet, is revered as the **Father of modern Malayalam literature**. He is credited with popularizing the **Arya Ezhuthu** script through his translation of the **Ramayana** (**Adhyathmaramayanam Kilippattu**).
 
• The **Vazhappally Inscription** is the oldest available lithic record of **Malayalam**, written in the **Vatteluttu** script during the reign of **Chera Perumal** King **Rajashekhara Varman**.
 
• The linguistic identity of **Malayalam** is distinct from **Tamil** despite their shared **Dravidian** roots, with **Malayalam** exhibiting unique features such as the loss of personal endings in verbs and a heavy influence of **Sanskrit** vocabulary.
 
• The **8th Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** currently lists **22 languages**, including all the **Classical Languages**, which provides them with official institutional support and promotion.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles was inserted into the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution by the Constitution (Ninety-seventh Amendment) Act of 2011?

options.text: Article 43A - Participation of workers in management of industries
Article 48A - Protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wild life
Article 39A - Equal justice and free legal aid

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 43B - Promotion of co-operative societies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution (Ninety-seventh Amendment) Act** of **2011** was enacted to provide constitutional status and protection to **co-operative societies**. It inserted **Article 43B** into the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Article 43B** mandates that the State shall endeavour to promote **voluntary formation**, **autonomous functioning**, **democratic control**, and **professional management** of **co-operative societies**.
 
• **Article 43A**, which deals with the **participation of workers in the management of industries**, was inserted by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act** of **1976**, not the 97th. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Article 48A**, focusing on the **protection and improvement of the environment** and safeguarding of **forests and wildlife**, was added to the Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act** in **1976**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Article 39A** provides for **equal justice and free legal aid** to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities. This was also inserted by the **42nd Amendment Act** of **1976**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** are enumerated in **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution from **Article 36 to 51**. They are borrowed from the **Irish Constitution** of **1937**.
 
• The **97th Constitutional Amendment Act** of **2011** brought three significant changes to the Constitution:
 
 
• It made the **right to form co-operative societies** a **Fundamental Right** under **Article 19(1)(c)**.
 
• It included a new **Directive Principle of State Policy** on the promotion of co-operative societies as **Article 43B**.
 
• It added a new **Part IXB** in the Constitution, titled "**The Co-operative Societies**" (consisting of Articles **243ZH to 243ZT**).
 
 
 
• In **July 2021**, the **Supreme Court of India** upheld a **Gujarat High Court** verdict that struck down certain provisions of the **97th Amendment** (specifically Part IXB) as they were passed without the required ratification by **at least half of the State Legislatures**, though it remains valid for **Multi-State Co-operative Societies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, often called the "**Mini-Constitution**", added four new Directive Principles: **Article 39** (opportunities for healthy development of children), **Article 39A** (equal justice and free legal aid), **Article 43A** (participation of workers), and **Article 48A** (environment protection).
 
• The **44th Amendment Act, 1978** added one more Directive Principle, **Article 38(2)**, which requires the State to **minimize inequalities** in income, status, facilities, and opportunities.
 
• The **86th Amendment Act, 2002** changed the subject matter of **Article 45** and made **elementary education** a fundamental right under **Article 21A**. The revised Article 45 directs the State to provide **early childhood care and education** for all children until they complete the **age of six years**.
 
• The **DPSP** are **non-justiciable** in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation, yet they are **fundamental in the governance** of the country.

questions.question: Which among the following changes were made in the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act ?

options.text: Increased Lok Sabha seats from 525 to 545.
Introduction of Fundamental Duties under Article 51A.
Inserted Right to Privacy in the Article 21 of Indian Constitution.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Introduction of Fundamental Duties under Article 51A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976** was enacted during the **Internal Emergency** (**1975-1977**) by the **Indira Gandhi** government and is often described as the **"Mini-Constitution"** due to the vast changes it brought to the **Constitution of India**.
 
• It introduced a new **Part IV-A** to the **Constitution**, which consisted of **Article 51A**. This article enumerated **10 Fundamental Duties** for the citizens, based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• The **31st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1973** increased the **Lok Sabha** seats from **525 to 545** to account for the population growth revealed in the **1971 Census**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• While the **42nd Amendment** did add several laws to the **9th Schedule** to protect them from **judicial review**, the comprehensive **Nationalization of Land Ceiling Laws** was not a singular defining feature of this amendment; such reforms were initiated through the **1st, 4th, and 17th Amendments**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• The **Right to Privacy** was declared a **Fundamental Right** under **Article 21** of the **Constitution** by the **Supreme Court** in the landmark **Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India** case in **2017**, not by the **42nd Amendment**. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Changes to the Preamble**:

 
 
• The **42nd Amendment** is the only amendment to have modified the **Preamble** of India. It added three new words: **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity**.
 
• It changed the description of India from a "**Sovereign Democratic Republic**" to a "**Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic**."
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A)**:
 
 
• Initially, there were **10 Fundamental Duties**. The **11th Fundamental Duty** (providing education opportunities to children aged **6 to 14 years**) was added later by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**.
 
• These duties are **non-justiciable**, meaning they cannot be enforced directly by the **courts**, though they serve as a guide for **citizens**.
 
 
 
• **Transfer of Subjects**:
 
 
• This amendment transferred **5 subjects** from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**: **Education**, **Forests**, **Weights and Measures**, **Protection of Wild Animals and Birds**, and **Administration of Justice**.
 
 
 
• **Duration of Legislatures**:
 
 
• The **42nd Amendment** extended the tenure of the **Lok Sabha** and the **State Legislative Assemblies** from **5 years to 6 years**. However, this change was later reversed by the **44th Amendment Act, 1978**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**:

 
 
• The amendment added **four new Directive Principles**: **Article 39** (opportunities for healthy development of children), **Article 39A** (**Equal justice and free legal aid**), **Article 43A** (participation of workers in management of industries), and **Article 48A** (protection of **environment** and **forests**).
 
 
 
• **Judicial Powers**:
 
 
• It sought to curtail the power of the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts** regarding **judicial review** and **writ jurisdiction**. Many of these restrictive provisions were subsequently struck down or repealed by the **43rd** and **44th Amendments** to restore **democracy** and **judicial independence**.
 
 
 
• **Presidential Obligations**:
 
 
• It made the **President** bound by the **advice** of the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Prime Minister**.

questions.question: Trisha and Riya started a partnership business, investing some amount in the ratio of 8 : 5. Poorva joined then after six months with an amount equal to that of Riya. In what ratio should the profit at the end of one year be distributed among Trisha, Riya and Poorva?
